messages:
alex: Heads-up — proposing a change to how we compute the fleet SLO pulse rollup to cut Prom ingestion + speed up EB reports. Quick summary: downsample 1m -> 5m, drop low-cardinality debug tags, and add a nightly aggregated bucket. Local sim showed ~28–35% ingestion reduction and much faster EB query times.

chris: can you show the current problem? numbers + concrete rules?

alex: current issue: we store slo burn metrics with tags: tenant, region, pool, gpu_family, model_hash, instance_size, request_path. cardinality explodes during rollout windows and when model variants churn. Prom scrape cardinality -> timeseries explosion.

alex: example of what we emit today:
```
fleet_slo_burn{tenant="acme",region="us-west-2",pool="dedicated-a",gpu_family="a100",model="gptx-v2",path="/v1/generate"} 0.04
```

alex: proposal (high level):
- recording rules to aggregate across model/version where possible (model->model_family)
- drop request_path except for global top-100 routes
- downsample burn windows to 5m for day-to-day EB, keep 1m for 1h hot window
- produce a nightly rollup metric fleet_slo_burn:daily that is compacted for long-term reports

priya: curious — how will this affect SLO alerting sensitivity? we don’t want to miss short spikes that cost error budget.

alex: good point. plan keeps a 1m-resolution hot window for last 60m (only aggregated by region+pool), so short spikes trigger alerts. the 5m downsample is used for the 6h/24h burn reports and the EB export.

marta: can you paste a candidate Prom recording rule and example Grafana query?

alex: yup — candidate recording rule (Prometheus):
```
- record: slo:burn_rate:5m
  expr: avg_over_time(fleet_slo_burn[5m])
  labels:
    resolution: "5m"
    compacted: "true"
```
and a rule to map model->family: 
```
- record: slo:model_family
  expr: label_replace(model_info{job="model-metadata"}, "model_family", "$1", "model", "(gptx-.*)-v.*")
```

alex: Grafana example for daily EB chart: 
- query: sum by (region, pool) (slo:burn_rate:5m{compacted="true"})
- display: rolling 24h burn with error-budget remaining line

chris: ok. what about alerting rules thresholds? do we need to tweak burn-rate windows?

priya: i’d keep current alert thresholds but route them to a separate burn-alert channel for 5m -> prevents noise. Only escalate from the 1m hot-window alerts.

alex: exactly. suggested config:
- hot alert: slo:hot_burn:1m > 1.0 for 3 consecutive 1m samples -> page
- rolling alert: slo:burn_rate:5m > 0.5 for 30m -> notify eng-sre but not page

marta: any cost estimate? what does 30% ingestion reduction mean in dollars?

alex: rough: our Prom ingest is ~120k series/day from burn metrics. compacting reduces to ~85k. on our bill that’s ~ $1.6k/month savings projected if we run fleet-wide. plus Grafana queries for EB exports are faster (reduced query time from 6m -> 40s in my test).

chris: important: we must preserve tenant-level billing accuracy for dedicated customers. how do we keep that after compacting?

alex: plan: keep raw 1m series for committed Dedicated tenants and for any active canary tenant for 24h. compact everything else. recording rules will maintain tenant labels for Dedicated-only series.

priya: rollout plan?

alex: proposal: staged:
1) dev environment testing of recording rules (this week)
2) prod trial in us-west-2 on non-dedicated tenants for 48h, fallback via feature-flagged recording rules (next week)
3) expand to other regions if no regressions (2 weeks)
4) nightly rollup enablement + EB export switch (4 weeks)

marta: can we add a telemetry validation job that compares old vs new EB numbers during trial? automated assert to avoid drift.

alex: yes — I added a small check: run pairwise queries (raw 1m vs compacted 5m) for 12h and assert <2% drift on 24h burn totals per region (fail -> auto rollback).

oncall-bot: NOTE: oncall window 2027-03-01 00:00 UTC -> 2027-03-08 00:00 UTC. Any changes that can page must be run outside oncall.

chris: good catch. schedule the prod trial for next Monday 16:00 UTC to avoid the oncall window.

priya: +1. Also add a Grafana dashboard diff panel so PMs can verify that product SLOs look identical in the trial.

alex: will prepare PR with recording rules, Grafana dashboard patch, and the validation job. tagging @chris @priya for review. trial run planned Mon 2173530000-2173538640 (est).

marta: thanks — appreciate the concise plan. keeping an eye on model-family mapping correctness.

alex: thx. will post PR link and followups here. :thumbsup:
